walkthroughs.body_html:
Applied Methods of Sociological Enquiry — a core area of GCSE Sociology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Applied Methods of Sociological Enquiry brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Applied Methods of Sociological Enquiry.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

Verstehen

Experiment

mcqs.q: What is the postmodern view of identity?
options: Identities are fluid, fragmented, and constructed through consumption and choice.
Everyone has the same identity in postmodern society.
Identity is fixed by class, gender, and ethnicity at birth.
Because they hate qualitative research.

mcqs.q: Why do positivists and interpretivists prefer different methods?
options: Both positivists and interpretivists prefer experiments above all else.
Positivists like numbers and interpretivists like words — that's the whole difference.

Positivists treat sociology like natural science, seeking objective measurable patterns — preferring quantitative methods. Interpretivists believe humans construct meaning, requiring qualitative methods to access subjective experience.
Because they hate qualitative research.

mcqs.q: Why do positivists prefer quantitative methods?
options: They produce objective, reliable, generalisable data resembling natural science.
Because numbers are easier to collect than words.
Because they hate qualitative research.
Both positivists and interpretivists prefer experiments above all else.
